│                                                                   │
│  📁 Navigator Panel (Left):                                      │
│  ├── Projects                                                   │
│  ├── TestSuites                                                 │
│  └── Interfaces                                                 │
│                                                                   │
│  📝 Editor Panel (Center):                                      │
│  ├── Request/Response View                                      │
│  ├── Test Editor                                                │
│  └── Assertions                                                 │
│                                                                   │
│  📊 Properties Panel (Right):                                   │
│  ├── Component Properties                                       │
│  ├── Project Properties                                         │
│  └── Global Properties                                          │
│                                                                   │
│  📋 Log Panel (Bottom):                                         │
│  ├── Script Log                                                 │
│  ├── HTTP Log                                                   │
│  └── Error Log                                                  │
│                                                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Initial Configuration**

```
File → Preferences →

🔧 Global Settings:
- Memory: Increase if testing large responses (e.g., -Xmx1024m)
- SSL: Import certificates if needed
- Proxy: Configure corporate proxy

📝 Editor Settings:
- Line numbers: Enable
- XML formatting: Pretty print
- Response timeout: 60000ms

🌐 HTTP Settings:
- Max redirects: 5
- Chunking: Disable if issues
- Keep-alive: Enable for performance
```

**Creating Your First Project**

**Method 1: From WSDL (SOAP)**

```
1. File → New SOAP Project
2. Project Name: "CalculatorAPI"
3. Initial WSDL: "http://www.dneonline.com/calculator.asmx?WSDL"
4. Check:
   ✓ Create Requests
   ✓ Create TestSuite
5. Click OK
```

**Method 2: From Swagger/OpenAPI (REST)**

```
1. File → New REST Project
2. Enter Swagger URL or paste JSON/YAML
3. Or: Import → Swagger/OpenAPI
4. Select endpoints to generate requests
```

**Method 3: Manual Creation**

```
1. File → New Project
2. Name: "MyAPIProject"
3. Right-click on project → New REST Service
4. Define base path: "https://api.example.com/v1"
5. Add resources: "/users", "/products"
```

**First Request**

```
# REST Request
1. Expand your project → REST Service → Resource → Method (GET)
2. Double-click request to open
3. Click ▶️ (green arrow) to run
4. View response in bottom panel

# SOAP Request
1. Expand Binding → Operation → Request
2. Fill in request XML
3. Click ▶️ to submit
```

**Sample REST Request**

```http
GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1
Headers:
  Accept: application/json
  Content-Type: application/json
```

**Sample SOAP Request**

```xml
<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
                  xmlns:tem="http://tempuri.org/">
   <soapenv:Header/>
   <soapenv:Body>
      <tem:Add>
         <tem:intA>10</tem:intA>
         <tem:intB>5</tem:intB>
      </tem:Add>
   </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>
```

**Key Insight:** SoapUI's project-based organization keeps all your API tests, assertions, and configurations in one place. Whether you're testing one endpoint or a hundred, the hierarchical structure (Project → TestSuite → TestCase → TestStep) keeps everything organized and maintainable.

content.title: Understanding SoapUI's Hierarchical Organization
content.explanation:
SoapUI uses a clear hierarchical structure to organize all testing artifacts. Understanding this structure is key to building maintainable test suites.

**The SoapUI Hierarchy**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SOAPUI HIERARCHY                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                   │
│  📁 Workspace                                                    │
│  ├── 📁 Project 1                                                │
│  │   ├── 📁 TestSuite 1                                          │
│  │   │   ├── 📁 TestCase 1                                       │
│  │   │   │   ├── 📄 TestStep 1 (REST Request)                    │
│  │   │   │   ├── 📄 TestStep 2 (Assertions)                      │
│  │   │   │   └── 📄 TestStep 3 (Property Transfer)               │
│  │   │   │                                                       │
│  │   │   └── 📁 TestCase 2                                       │
│  │   │                                                           │
│  │   ├── 📁 MockService                                          │
│  │   └── 📁 LoadTest                                             │
│  │                                                               │
│  └── 📁 Project 2                                                │
│                                                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Workspace Level**

- Contains multiple projects
- Persists global settings
- `.workspace` file

```xml
<soapui:workspace name="Default Workspace">
    <project>file:/C:/projects/UserAPI.xml</project>
    <project>file:/C:/projects/OrderAPI.xml</project>
</soapui:workspace>
```

**Project Level**

A project represents an API or application under test:

```xml
<soapui:project name="UserAPI" resourceRoot="C:/projects/UserAPI">
    <properties>
        <property name="baseUrl" value="https://api.example.com/v1"/>
        <property name="apiKey" value="${#Project#apiKey}"/>
    </properties>
    
    <interface>...</interface>
    <testSuite>...</testSuite>
    <mockService>...</mockService>
</soapui:project>
```

**Project Components**

| Component | Purpose | Icon |
|-----------|---------|------|
| **Interfaces** | API definitions (WSDL/Swagger) | 🌐 |
| **TestSuites** | Collection of test cases | 📋 |
| **MockServices** | Simulated API endpoints | 🎭 |
| **LoadTests** | Performance test configurations | ⚡ |
| **SecurityTests** | Vulnerability scans | 🔒 |

**Interfaces and Operations**

When you import a WSDL or Swagger, SoapUI creates:

```
REST Service: Users
├── Resource: /users
│   ├── Method: GET (Get all users)
│   ├── Method: POST (Create user)
│   └── Method: DELETE (Delete all)
└── Resource: /users/{id}
    ├── Method: GET (Get user)
    ├── Method: PUT (Update user)
    └── Method: DELETE (Delete user)
```

**TestSuite Structure**

A TestSuite groups related test cases:

```xml
<testSuite name="UserAPITestSuite">
    <properties>
        <property name="testUserId" value=""/>
    </properties>
    
    <testCase name="CreateUserTest">...</testCase>
    <testCase name="GetUserTest">...</testCase>
    <testCase name="UpdateUserTest">...</testCase>
    <testCase name="DeleteUserTest">...</testCase>
</testSuite>
```

**TestCase Structure**

A TestCase contains TestSteps executed in order:

```xml
<testCase name="CreateUserTest">
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="CreateUserRequest">
        <config>...</config>
    </testStep>
    
    <testStep type="groovy" name="ExtractID">
        <script>...</script>
    </testStep>
    
    <testStep type="propertystransfer" name="TransferID">
        <transfer>...</transfer>
    </testStep>
</testCase>
```

**Properties: The Glue**

Properties are variables that can be used throughout SoapUI:

```
#Project Level
${#Project#baseUrl}
${#Project#apiKey}

#TestSuite Level
${#TestSuite#userId}
${#TestSuite#authToken}

#TestCase Level
${#TestCase#orderId}
${#TestCase#timestamp}

#Global Properties
${#System#os.name}
${#Env#PATH}

#Custom Property Expansion
${#Project#baseUrl}/users/${#TestSuite#userId}
```

**Setting Properties**

```
1. Right-click project → Properties
2. Add property name and value
3. Use in requests: ${#Project#propertyName}

Dynamically via Groovy:
def userId = context.expand('${#TestCase#userId}')
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue("status", "active")
```

**Property Transfer TestStep**

This special step transfers values between responses and properties:

```
Property Transfer Configuration:

Source: CreateUser Response
├── Property: Response
└── XPath: //userId

Target: TestSuite Properties
├── Property: userId
└── Transfer Type: Set
```

**Project File Structure**

Projects are stored as XML files:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<con:soapui-project id="123" name="UserAPI"
    xmlns:con="http://eviware.com/soapui/config">
    
    <con:properties>
        <con:property>
            <con:name>baseUrl</con:name>
            <con:value>https://api.example.com</con:value>
        </con:property>
    </con:properties>
    
    <con:interface xsi:type="con:RestService" name="UsersAPI">
        <con:endpoints>
            <con:endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</con:endpoint>
        </con:endpoints>
        <con:resource name="Users" path="/users">
            <con:method name="GET" method="GET"/>
        </con:resource>
    </con:interface>
    
    <con:testSuite name="UserTests">
        <con:testCase name="GetAllUsers">
            <con:testStep type="restrequest" name="GetRequest">
                <con:config>
                    <con:restMethod>GET</con:restMethod>
                    <con:endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</con:endpoint>
                    <con:resourcePath>/users</con:resourcePath>
                </con:config>
            </con:testStep>
        </con:testCase>
    </con:testSuite>
</con:soapui-project>
```

**Best Practices for Project Structure**

| Practice | Why | How |
|----------|-----|-----|
| **Use meaningful names** | Clarity | `CreateUser_ValidData` not `Test1` |
| **Leverage properties** | DRY principle | Store URLs, credentials, IDs |
| **Group by functionality** | Organization | TestSuite per API resource |
| **Version control projects** | History | Store `.xml` files in Git |
| **Use externalize test data** | Maintainability | Properties files, Excel |

**Key Insight:** The hierarchical structure of SoapUI isn't just organization—it's a powerful framework for reusability. Properties at different levels let you control scope, while the TestStep sequence gives you complete control over test flow. Master this structure, and you can build complex test suites that are still maintainable.

content.title: Building Comprehensive Test Cases
content.explanation:
Test Cases are the heart of SoapUI testing. They contain ordered TestSteps that execute sequentially, allowing you to build complex test scenarios.

**Creating a Test Case**

```
1. Right-click TestSuite → New TestCase
2. Name: "Create User Flow"
3. Description: "Complete user creation flow with validation"
4. Properties: Add test-specific properties
```

**Available TestStep Types**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      TESTSTEP TYPES                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                   │
│  🖧 HTTP Requests:                                                │
│  ├── REST Request                                                │
│  ├── SOAP Request                                                │
│  ├── HTTP Request (Generic)                                      │
│  └── AMF Request                                                 │
│                                                                   │
│  🔄 Flow Control:                                                │
│  ├── Conditional Goto                                            │
│  ├── Run TestCase                                                │
│  ├── Delay                                                       │
│  └── Property Transfer                                           │
│                                                                   │
│  📊 Data Sources:                                                │
│  ├── Data Source (Excel, CSV, JDBC)                              │
│  ├── Data Source Loop                                            │
│  └── Data Sink                                                   │
│                                                                   │
│  📝 Scripting:                                                   │
│  ├── Groovy Script                                               │
│  └── Script Assertion                                            │
│                                                                   │
│  🛡️ Security:                                                    │
│  ├── Security Test                                               │
│  └── Malformed XML/SQL Injection                                 │
│                                                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Complete User CRUD Test Case Example**

```xml
<testCase name="UserCRUD" failOnError="true">
    
    <!-- Step 1: Create User -->
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Create User">
        <config>
            <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</endpoint>
            <resource>/users</resource>
            <method>POST</method>
            <request>
            {
                "name": "John Doe",
                "email": "john@example.com",
                "age": 30
            }
            </request>
        </config>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
            <configuration>
                <codes>201</codes>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 2: Extract User ID -->
    <testStep type="groovy" name="Extract User ID">
        <script>
            // Get response
            def response = context.expand('${Create User#Response}')
            def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
            
            // Store in test case properties
            testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue("userId", json.id.toString())
            log.info "User ID: ${json.id}"
        </script>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 3: Get User -->
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Get User">
        <config>
            <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</endpoint>
            <resource>/users/${#TestCase#userId}</resource>
            <method>GET</method>
        </config>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
            <configuration>
                <codes>200</codes>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Existence">
            <configuration>
                <path>$.name</path>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 4: Update User -->
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Update User">
        <config>
            <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</endpoint>
            <resource>/users/${#TestCase#userId}</resource>
            <method>PUT</method>
            <request>
            {
                "name": "John Updated",
                "email": "john.updated@example.com",
                "age": 31
            }
            </request>
        </config>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
            <configuration>
                <codes>200</codes>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 5: Verify Update -->
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Verify Update">
        <config>
            <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</endpoint>
            <resource>/users/${#TestCase#userId}</resource>
            <method>GET</method>
        </config>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Match">
            <configuration>
                <path>$.name</path>
                <value>John Updated</value>
                <allowWildcards>false</allowWildcards>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 6: Delete User -->
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Delete User">
        <config>
            <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</endpoint>
            <resource>/users/${#TestCase#userId}</resource>
            <method>DELETE</method>
        </config>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
            <configuration>
                <codes>204</codes>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 7: Verify Deletion -->
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Verify Deletion">
        <config>
            <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</endpoint>
            <resource>/users/${#TestCase#userId}</resource>
            <method>GET</method>
        </config>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
            <configuration>
                <codes>404</codes>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
</testCase>
```

**Conditional Logic with Goto**

```xml
<!-- Conditional execution based on response -->
<testStep type="goto" name="Check Status">
    <condition>
        <expression>${Create User#Response#status} == 201</expression>
        <targetStep>Extract User ID</targetStep>
    </condition>
    <condition>
        <expression>true</expression>
        <targetStep>Handle Error</targetStep>
    </condition>
</testStep>
```

**Running Test Cases Sequentially**

```xml
<!-- Run another test case within this test case -->
<testStep type="runTestCase" name="Run Auth Test">
    <targetTestCase>Authentication Tests</targetTestCase>
    <properties>
        <property name="username" value="admin"/>
        <property name="password" value="password"/>
    </properties>
</testStep>
```

**Delays for Realistic Pacing**

```xml
<testStep type="delay" name="Think Time">
    <delay>2000</delay> <!-- 2 seconds -->
</testStep>
```

**Data-Driven Testing with DataSource**

```xml
<!-- Excel DataSource -->
<testStep type="datasource" name="Excel Data">
    <config>
        <driver>Excel</driver>
        <file>C:/testdata/users.xlsx</file>
        <sheet>Sheet1</sheet>
        <properties>
            <property>name</property>
            <property>email</property>
            <property>age</property>
        </properties>
    </config>
</testStep>

<!-- Loop through data -->
<testStep type="datasourceLoop" name="Process Each Row">
    <dataSource>Excel Data</dataSource>
    <!-- Steps here execute for each row -->
</testStep>

<!-- Create user with current row data -->
<testStep type="restrequest" name="Create User">
    <config>
        <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</endpoint>
        <resource>/users</resource>
        <method>POST</method>
        <request>
        {
            "name": "${#DataSource#name}",
            "email": "${#DataSource#email}",
            "age": ${#DataSource#age}
        }
        </request>
    </config>
</testStep>

<!-- DataSink to save results -->
<testStep type="datasink" name="Save Results">
    <dataSource>Excel Data</dataSource>
    <target>C:/testdata/results.xlsx</target>
    <properties>
        <property name="status" value="${Create User#Response#status}"/>
    </properties>
</testStep>
```

**Test Case Properties**

Properties can be defined at test case level:

```xml
<testCase name="UserCRUD" failOnError="true">
    <properties>
        <property name="userId" value=""/>
        <property name="authToken" value="${#TestSuite#authToken}"/>
        <property name="timestamp" value=""/>
    </properties>
    <!-- Steps -->
</testCase>
```

**Setting Properties at Runtime**

```groovy
// Groovy script to set properties
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat

// Generate timestamp
def dateFormat = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'")
dateFormat.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC"))

// Set test case property
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue("timestamp", dateFormat.format(new Date()))

// Set test suite property
testRunner.testCase.testSuite.setPropertyValue("lastRun", new Date().toString())

// Set project property
testRunner.testCase.testSuite.project.setPropertyValue("lastUserId", userId)

// Access properties
def userId = testRunner.testCase.getPropertyValue("userId")
log.info "Current user: ${userId}"
```

**Test Case Execution Options**

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Fail on Error** | Stop test case if any step fails |
| **Ignore Errors** | Continue despite failures |
| **Max Steps** | Prevent infinite loops |
| **Timeout** | Overall test case timeout |
| **Keep Session** | Maintain HTTP session across steps |

**Running Test Cases**

```
# From UI
Right-click TestCase → Run TestCase

# From command line
```bash
testrunner.sh -f reports/ UserAPI-soapui-project.xml
```

**Test Case Reports**

After execution, SoapUI generates:

- **JUnit-style XML** for CI/CD integration
- **HTML reports** with step-by-step results
- **Transaction logs** for debugging

**Key Insight:** Test Cases in SoapUI are like mini-programs. With conditional logic, data sources, and scripting, you can simulate almost any real-world scenario. The sequential nature makes debugging intuitive—you can see exactly where a test failed and why.

content.title: Comprehensive Response Validation
content.explanation:
Assertions are how SoapUI verifies that responses meet expectations. With over 50 built-in assertion types, you can validate virtually every aspect of an API response.

**Adding Assertions**

```
1. Open a TestStep (REST/SOAP request)
2. Click the Assertions tab (bottom of request editor)
3. Click + (Add Assertion) button
4. Select assertion category and type
5. Configure assertion parameters
```

**Assertion Categories**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      ASSERTION CATEGORIES                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                   │
│  📝 Content:                                                     │
│  ├── Contains                                                    │
│  ├── Not Contains                                                │
│  ├── XPath Match                                                 │
│  ├── XQuery Match                                                │
│  └── JSONPath Existence                                          │
│                                                                   │
│  🌐 HTTP:                                                        │
│  ├── Valid HTTP Status Codes                                     │
│  ├── Invalid HTTP Status Codes                                   │
│  ├── Response SLA                                                │
│  ├── Response Headers                                            │
│  └── Response Size                                               │
│                                                                   │
│  🔒 Security:                                                    │
│  ├── Sensitive Information Exposure                              │
│  ├── Malformed XML/SQL Injection                                 │
│  └── XPath Injection                                             │
│                                                                   │
│  📊 Compliance:                                                  │
│  ├── Schema Compliance                                           │
│  ├── WS-I Compliance                                             │
│  └── WSDL Compliance                                             │
│                                                                   │
│  📋 Script:                                                      │
│  ├── Script Assertion                                            │
│  └── Groovy Script Assertion                                     │
│                                                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Essential HTTP Assertions**

```xml
<!-- Status Code Assertion -->
<assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
    <configuration>
        <codes>200,201,202</codes>
        <ignore404>false</ignore404>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Response SLA (Performance) -->
<assertion type="Response SLA">
    <configuration>
        <sla>500</sla> <!-- milliseconds -->
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Response Headers -->
<assertion type="Response Headers">
    <configuration>
        <header>Content-Type</header>
        <value>application/json</value>
        <matchType>contains</matchType>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Response Size -->
<assertion type="Response Size">
    <configuration>
        <size>1024</size>
        <sizeType>lt</sizeType> <!-- lt, gt, eq -->
    </configuration>
</assertion>
```

**JSON Assertions**

```xml
<!-- JSONPath Existence -->
<assertion type="JSONPath Existence">
    <configuration>
        <path>$.user.id</path>
        <allowWildcards>true</allowWildcards>
        <expectedContent>?</expectedContent>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- JSONPath Match (exact value) -->
<assertion type="JSONPath Match">
    <configuration>
        <path>$.user.name</path>
        <value>John Doe</value>
        <allowWildcards>false</allowWildcards>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- JSONPath Count -->
<assertion type="JSONPath Count">
    <configuration>
        <path>$.orders[*]</path>
        <count>5</count>
        <allowWildcards>false</allowWildcards>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- JSONPath Regex -->
<assertion type="JSONPath Match">
    <configuration>
        <path>$.user.email</path>
        <value>^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$</value>
        <allowWildcards>true</allowWildcards> <!-- Enable regex -->
    </configuration>
</assertion>
```

**XML Assertions (for SOAP)**

```xml
<!-- XPath Match -->
<assertion type="XPath Match">
    <configuration>
        <path>//user/name</path>
        <value>John Doe</value>
        <namespaceDeclarations>
            <ns1>http://example.com/user</ns1>
        </namespaceDeclarations>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- XPath Count -->
<assertion type="XPath Count">
    <configuration>
        <path>//order</path>
        <count>3</count>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Contains -->
<assertion type="Contains">
    <configuration>
        <token>SUCCESS</token>
        <ignoreCase>false</ignoreCase>
        <useRegEx>false</useRegEx>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Not Contains -->
<assertion type="Not Contains">
    <configuration>
        <token>ERROR</token>
    </configuration>
</assertion>
```

**Schema Compliance Assertions**

```xml
<!-- REST Schema Compliance (JSON) -->
<assertion type="Schema Compliance">
    <configuration>
        <schemaDefinition>
            {
                "type": "object",
                "required": ["id", "name"],
                "properties": {
                    "id": {"type": "integer"},
                    "name": {"type": "string"}
                }
            }
        </schemaDefinition>
        <definitionType>JSON</definitionType>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- SOAP Schema Compliance -->
<assertion type="Schema Compliance">
    <configuration>
        <definitionType>WSDL</definitionType>
        <wsdlUrl>http://example.com/service?wsdl</wsdlUrl>
    </configuration>
</assertion>
```

**Script Assertions (Groovy)**

For complex validation logic that built-in assertions can't handle:

```groovy
// Script Assertion
import groovy.json.JsonSlurper

// Parse response
def response = messageExchange.responseContent
def json = new JsonSlurper().parseText(response)

// Custom validation
def hasValidAge = json.age >= 18 && json.age <= 100
assert hasValidAge : "Age ${json.age} is outside valid range"

// Business logic validation
if (json.role == 'admin') {
    assert json.permissions.contains('ALL') : "Admin missing ALL permissions"
}

// Cross-field validation
if (json.age < 18) {
    assert json.hasParent == true : "Minor missing parent flag"
}

// Check if email domain is allowed
allowedDomains = ['example.com', 'test.org']
def emailDomain = json.email.split('@')[1]
assert allowedDomains.contains(emailDomain) : "Domain ${emailDomain} not allowed"

// Log for debugging
log.info "Validated user: ${json.name}"
```

**Advanced Script Assertion**

```groovy
// Script Assertion with multiple validations
import groovy.json.JsonSlurper

// Get response data
def response = messageExchange.responseContent
def json = new JsonSlurper().parseText(response)

// Get request data (for comparison)
def request = messageExchange.requestContent
def requestJson = new JsonSlurper().parseText(request)

// Track failures
List failures = []

// Validate response structure
if (!json.id) {
    failures.add("Missing id field")
}

// Validate data consistency
if (json.name != requestJson.name) {
    failures.add("Name mismatch: expected ${requestJson.name}, got ${json.name}")
}

// Validate timestamps
def created = Date.parse("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'", json.createdAt)
def now = new Date()
if (created > now) {
    failures.add("Created date is in the future")
}

// Validate numeric ranges
if (json.age < 0 || json.age > 150) {
    failures.add("Age ${json.age} out of range")
}

// Fail if any issues found
if (failures) {
    assert false : failures.join("\n")
}
```

**Assertion Configuration Tips**

| Assertion Type | Best Practice | Example |
|----------------|---------------|---------|
| **Status Code** | Always add | Check 200 for success, 400 for validation |
| **SLA** | Set realistic thresholds | 500ms for critical endpoints |
| **JSONPath** | Use regex for dynamic values | `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` for dates |
| **Contains** | Avoid for large responses | Use specific tokens only |
| **Script** | Only for complex logic | Business rules, cross-field validation |

**Multiple Assertions**

You can add multiple assertions to a single TestStep:

```xml
<testStep type="restrequest" name="Get User">
    <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
        <configuration><codes>200</codes></configuration>
    </assertion>
    <assertion type="Response SLA">
        <configuration><sla>300</sla></configuration>
    </assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Existence">
        <configuration><path>$.id</path></configuration>
    </assertion>
    <assertion type="JSONPath Match">
        <configuration>
            <path>$.name</path>
            <value>John</value>
        </configuration>
    </assertion>
    <assertion type="Response Headers">
        <configuration>
            <header>Content-Type</header>
            <value>application/json</value>
        </configuration>
    </assertion>
</testStep>
```

**Assertion Best Practices**

| Practice | Why |
|----------|-----|
| **Assert status codes first** | Basic validation before diving into content |
| **Use specific assertions** | JSONPath for JSON, XPath for XML |
| **Avoid over-asserting** | Test what matters, not everything |
| **Set realistic SLAs** | Based on actual performance requirements |
| **Combine with property transfer** | Validate dynamic values correctly |
| **Use script assertions sparingly** | They're powerful but harder to maintain |

**Key Insight:** Assertions transform requests into tests. SoapUI's extensive assertion library means you can validate everything from simple status codes to complex business rules. The key is choosing the right assertion for the job—use built-in assertions where possible, and reserve script assertions for truly custom logic.

content.title: Testing Database Interactions
content.explanation:
JDBC Request test steps allow you to query databases directly within your API tests. This is crucial for end-to-end testing, data verification, and test data setup/cleanup.

**Why Database Testing?**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    DATABASE TESTING BENEFITS                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                   │
│  ✅ Verify data persistence after API calls                       │
│  ✅ Set up test data before test execution                         │
│  ✅ Clean up test data after tests                                 │
│  ✅ Validate complex business rules at DB level                    │
│  ✅ Test stored procedures and views                               │
│  ✅ Verify data integrity across tables                            │
│                                                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Adding a JDBC Request TestStep**

```
1. Right-click TestCase → Add Step → JDBC Request
2. Configure database connection
3. Write SQL query
4. Add assertions on results
```

**Database Connection Configuration**

```xml
<testStep type="jdbc" name="Query Users">
    <config>
        <driver>com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver</driver>
        <connection>
            <url>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/testdb</url>
            <username>testuser</username>
            <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
        </connection>
        <query>SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${#TestCase#userId}</query>
        <properties>
            <property name="userId" value="${#TestCase#userId}"/>
        </properties>
    </config>
</testStep>
```

**Common JDBC Drivers**

| Database | Driver Class | URL Format |
|----------|--------------|------------|
| **MySQL** | `com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver` | `jdbc:mysql://host:3306/db` |
| **PostgreSQL** | `org.postgresql.Driver` | `jdbc:postgresql://host:5432/db` |
| **Oracle** | `oracle.jdbc.OracleDriver` | `jdbc:oracle:thin:@host:1521:sid` |
| **SQL Server** | `com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver` | `jdbc:sqlserver://host:1433;databaseName=db` |
| **H2** | `org.h2.Driver` | `jdbc:h2:~/test` |

**Example: Verify User Creation**

```xml
<testCase name="Verify User Creation">
    <!-- Step 1: Create user via API -->
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Create User API">
        <config>
            <endpoint>${#Project#baseUrl}</endpoint>
            <resource>/users</resource>
            <method>POST</method>
            <request>
            {
                "name": "John Doe",
                "email": "john@example.com"
            }
            </request>
        </config>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 2: Extract user ID from response -->
    <testStep type="groovy" name="Extract ID">
        <script>
            def response = context.expand('${Create User API#Response}')
            def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
            testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue("userId", json.id.toString())
        </script>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 3: Query database to verify -->
    <testStep type="jdbc" name="Verify in Database">
        <config>
            <driver>com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver</driver>
            <connection>
                <url>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/appdb</url>
                <username>appuser</username>
                <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
            </connection>
            <query>
                SELECT * FROM users 
                WHERE id = ${#TestCase#userId}
                AND name = 'John Doe'
                AND email = 'john@example.com'
            </query>
        </config>
        <assertion type="JDBC Status">
            <configuration>
                <rowCount>1</rowCount>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
</testCase>
```

**Example: Test Data Setup**

```xml
<testCase name="Setup Test Data">
    <!-- Insert test data before running tests -->
    <testStep type="jdbc" name="Insert Test User">
        <config>
            <driver>com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver</driver>
            <connection>
                <url>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/appdb</url>
                <username>appuser</username>
                <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
            </connection>
            <query>
                INSERT INTO users (name, email, role, created_at)
                VALUES (
                    'Test User',
                    'test@example.com',
                    'admin',
                    NOW()
                )
            </query>
        </config>
        <assertion type="JDBC Status">
            <configuration>
                <rowCount>1</rowCount>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Get the auto-generated ID -->
    <testStep type="jdbc" name="Get User ID">
        <config>
            <driver>com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver</driver>
            <connection>
                <url>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/appdb</url>
                <username>appuser</username>
                <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
            </connection>
            <query>
                SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID() as user_id
            </query>
        </config>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Extract ID to property -->
    <testStep type="propertyTransfer" name="Transfer ID">
        <transfers>
            <transfer>
                <sourceType>Response</sourceType>
                <sourceStep>Get User ID</sourceStep>
                <sourcePath>//user_id</sourcePath>
                <targetType>TestCase</targetType>
                <targetName>userId</targetName>
            </transfer>
        </transfers>
    </testStep>
</testCase>
```

**Example: Data Cleanup**

```xml
<testCase name="Cleanup Test Data">
    <!-- Delete test data after tests -->
    <testStep type="jdbc" name="Delete Test User">
        <config>
            <driver>com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver</driver>
            <connection>
                <url>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/appdb</url>
                <username>appuser</username>
                <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
            </connection>
            <query>
                DELETE FROM users 
                WHERE email LIKE 'test-%'
                OR created_at > DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
            </query>
        </config>
        <assertion type="JDBC Status">
            <configuration>
                <rowCount>-1</rowCount> <!-- Don't check exact count -->
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
</testCase>
```

**Example: Complex Business Validation**

```xml
<testStep type="jdbc" name="Validate Order Total">
    <config>
        <driver>com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver</driver>
        <connection>
            <url>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/appdb</url>
            <username>appuser</username>
            <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
        </connection>
        <query>
            SELECT 
                o.id as order_id,
                o.total as order_total,
                SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price) as calculated_total
            FROM orders o
            JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id
            WHERE o.id = ${#TestCase#orderId}
            GROUP BY o.id, o.total
        </query>
    </config>
    <assertion type="XPath Match">
        <configuration>
            <path>//calculated_total</path>
            <value>${#TestCase#orderTotal}</value>
        </configuration>
    </assertion>
</testStep>
```

**JDBC Assertions**

SoapUI provides several assertions for JDBC responses:

```xml
<!-- Check row count -->
<assertion type="JDBC Status">
    <configuration>
        <rowCount>5</rowCount>
        <comparator>=</comparator>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Check specific cell value -->
<assertion type="XPath Match">
    <configuration>
        <path>//row[1]/name</path>
        <value>John</value>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Check column exists -->
<assertion type="XPath Exists">
    <configuration>
        <path>//email</path>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Check for no results (when expected) -->
<assertion type="NotXPathExists">
    <configuration>
        <path>//row</path>
    </configuration>
</assertion>
```

**Handling Stored Procedures**

```xml
<!-- Call stored procedure -->
<testStep type="jdbc" name="Call SP">
    <config>
        <driver>com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver</driver>
        <connection>
            <url>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/appdb</url>
            <username>appuser</username>
            <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
        </connection>
        <query>
            CALL get_user_orders(
                ${#TestCase#userId},
                @order_count,
                @total_spent
            );
            SELECT @order_count as order_count,
                   @total_spent as total_spent;
        </query>
    </config>
</testStep>
```

**Parameterized Queries**

```xml
<!-- Safe parameterized queries prevent SQL injection -->
<testStep type="jdbc" name="Safe Query">
    <config>
        <driver>com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver</driver>
        <connection>
            <url>jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/appdb</url>
            <username>appuser</username>
            <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
        </connection>
        <query>
            SELECT * FROM users 
            WHERE name = ? AND email = ?
        </query>
        <parameters>
            <parameter>${#TestCase#userName}</parameter>
            <parameter>${#TestCase#userEmail}</parameter>
        </parameters>
    </config>
</testStep>
```

**JDBC Best Practices**

| Practice | Why |
|----------|-----|
| **Store credentials securely** | Use project properties or encrypted values |
| **Use parameterized queries** | Prevent SQL injection |
| **Clean up test data** | Avoid polluting database |
| **Use transactions when needed** | Maintain data consistency |
| **Close connections properly** | Prevent connection leaks |
| **Limit result sets** | Use WHERE clauses, LIMIT |
| **Test on non-production DB** | Never run on production |

**Troubleshooting JDBC Issues**

```groovy
// Groovy script to test connection
def driver = "com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"
def url = "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/testdb"
def user = "testuser"
def password = "testpass"

// Test connection
Class.forName(driver)
def conn = DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, password)
def stmt = conn.createStatement()
def rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT 1")
if (rs.next()) {
    log.info "Connection successful: ${rs.getInt(1)}"
}
conn.close()
```

**Key Insight:** JDBC Request steps bridge the gap between API tests and database verification. They enable true end-to-end testing—from API request to data persistence—and provide powerful capabilities for test data management. This is especially valuable for integration testing where data correctness is paramount.

content.title: Creating Virtual APIs with Mock Services
content.explanation:
Mock Services in SoapUI allow you to simulate API behavior before the actual API is built. This enables parallel development, testing in isolation, and simulating edge cases.

**Why Use Mock Services?**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    MOCK SERVICES BENEFITS                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                   │
│  🚀 Parallel Development: Frontend can start before backend       │
│  🧪 Isolated Testing: Test without external dependencies         │
│  🔄 Simulate Edge Cases: Errors, timeouts, rare responses         │
│  📚 Contract Testing: Verify API contracts before implementation  │
│  💰 Cost Savings: Avoid calling paid APIs during testing          │
│  🏗️ Demo Creation: Build demos without real backend              │
│                                                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Creating a Mock Service**

```
1. Right-click Project → New Mock Service
2. Name: "UserAPI Mock"
3. Port: 8080 (or any available port)
4. Path: /api/v1 (base path)
5. Click OK
```

**Mock Service Structure**

```
Mock Service: UserAPI Mock (Port: 8080)
├── Mock Operation: GET /users
│   ├── MockResponse: Success - Returns user list
│   └── MockResponse: Error - Returns 500
├── Mock Operation: GET /users/{id}
│   ├── MockResponse: Found - Returns single user
│   └── MockResponse: Not Found - Returns 404
└── Mock Operation: POST /users
    ├── MockResponse: Created - Returns 201
    └── MockResponse: Validation Error - Returns 400
```

**Adding Mock Operations**

```
1. Right-click Mock Service → New Mock Operation
2. Select operation from interface (or create custom)
3. Add multiple mock responses for different scenarios
```

**Mock Response Configuration**

```xml
<mockResponse name="Success Response"
              id="123"
              httpResponseStatus="200"
              responseDelay="100">
    
    <!-- Response Headers -->
    <headers>
        <header name="Content-Type" value="application/json"/>
        <header name="Cache-Control" value="no-cache"/>
    </headers>
    
    <!-- Response Body -->
    <content><![CDATA[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "John Doe",
        "email": "john@example.com"
    }
    ]]></content>
    
    <!-- Script to run when this response is used -->
    <script>
        log.info "Serving success response for user 1"
    </script>
</mockResponse>
```

**Dynamic Responses with Scripting**

```groovy
// Groovy script in mock response
import groovy.json.JsonBuilder
import groovy.json.JsonSlurper

// Parse request if needed
def requestContent = mockRequest.requestContent
def requestJson = requestContent ? new JsonSlurper().parseText(requestContent) : [:]

// Dynamic response based on request
if (requestJson.name && requestJson.email) {
    // Success case
    def response = [
        id: new Random().nextInt(1000),
        name: requestJson.name,
        email: requestJson.email,
        created: new Date().format("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'", TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC"))
    ]
    
    mockResponse.responseContent = new JsonBuilder(response).toPrettyString()
    mockResponse.responseHttpStatus = 201
} else {
    // Error case
    def error = [
        error: "Validation Error",
        details: "Name and email are required"
    ]
    
    mockResponse.responseContent = new JsonBuilder(error).toPrettyString()
    mockResponse.responseHttpStatus = 400
}
```

**Conditional Mock Responses**

```groovy
// Script to select which response to return
def request = mockRequest.requestContent
def userId = mockRequest.getPath().split('/').last()

if (userId == '1') {
    return "Success Response"  // Return specific mock response
} else if (userId == '999') {
    return "Not Found Response"
} else if (userId == '500') {
    return "Error Response"
} else {
    // Default response
    return "Generic Response"
}
```

**Dynamic Response Based on Request Headers**

```groovy
// Check request headers
def authHeader = mockRequest.getRequestHeaders()['Authorization']
if (authHeader && authHeader[0] == 'Bearer valid-token') {
    return "Authenticated Response"
} else {
    mockResponse.responseHttpStatus = 401
    mockResponse.responseContent = '{"error":"Unauthorized"}'
}
```

**Simulating Delays and Timeouts**

```xml
<!-- Delayed response -->
<mockResponse name="Slow Response"
              httpResponseStatus="200"
              responseDelay="5000"> <!-- 5 second delay -->
    <content><![CDATA[
    {
        "status": "processing",
        "message": "This might take a while"
    }
    ]]></content>
</mockResponse>
```

**Stateful Mock Services**

```groovy
// Maintain state between requests
import groovy.json.JsonSlurper

// Initialize storage (static variable persists)
if (!context.storage) {
    context.storage = [
        users: [:],
        nextId: 1
    ]
}

def method = mockRequest.method

def handleRequest() {
    switch(method) {
        case 'POST':
            // Create user
            def request = new JsonSlurper().parseText(mockRequest.requestContent)
            def id = context.storage.nextId++
            context.storage.users[id] = request
            
            mockResponse.responseHttpStatus = 201
            mockResponse.responseContent = new JsonBuilder([id: id] + request).toPrettyString()
            break
            
        case 'GET':
            // Get user
            def userId = mockRequest.getPath().split('/').last() as Integer
            def user = context.storage.users[userId]
            
            if (user) {
                mockResponse.responseHttpStatus = 200
                mockResponse.responseContent = new JsonBuilder(user).toPrettyString()
            } else {
                mockResponse.responseHttpStatus = 404
                mockResponse.responseContent = '{"error":"User not found"}'
            }
            break
    }
}
```

**Starting Mock Services**

```
# From UI
Right-click Mock Service → Start

# From command line
```bash
mockservicerunner.sh -m "UserAPI Mock" UserAPI-soapui-project.xml
```

**Using Mocks in Tests**

```xml
<testCase name="Test with Mock">
    <!-- Start mock if not running -->
    <testStep type="groovy" name="Start Mock">
        <script>
            def mockService = testRunner.testCase.testSuite.project
                .getMockServiceByName("UserAPI Mock")
            if (!mockService.running) {
                mockService.start()
            }
        </script>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Call mock instead of real API -->
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Call Mock">
        <config>
            <endpoint>http://localhost:8080/api/v1</endpoint>
            <resource>/users/1</resource>
            <method>GET</method>
        </config>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
            <configuration>
                <codes>200</codes>
            </configuration>
        </assertion>
    </testStep>
</testCase>
```

**Mock Service Advanced Features**

| Feature | Description | Use Case |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| **Scripting** | Groovy scripts for dynamic responses | Complex logic, stateful mocks |
| **Dispatching** | Choose response based on request | Simulate different scenarios |
| **Delays** | Programmatic or fixed delays | Performance testing, timeouts |
| **Headers** | Custom response headers | Test header-dependent clients |
| **SSL** | HTTPS support | Secure API mocking |
| **Multiple Ports** | Run multiple mocks | Simulate microservices |

**Mock Service Dispatching Options**

```
Right-click Mock Operation → Show Mock Operation Editor → Dispatch

Options:
- SEQUENCE: Cycle through responses in order
- RANDOM: Randomly select response
- SCRIPT: Groovy script to choose response
- QUERY_MATCH: Match based on request parameters
- XPATH_MATCH: Match based on XPath
- JSONPATH_MATCH: Match based on JSONPath
```

**JSONPath Match Dispatching**

```xml
<dispatchConfig type="JSONPATH_MATCH">
    <dispatchOptions>
        <dispatchOption>
            <jsonpath>$.user.role</jsonpath>
            <value>admin</value>
            <response>Admin Response</response>
        </dispatchOption>
        <dispatchOption>
            <jsonpath>$.user.role</jsonpath>
            <value>user</value>
            <response>User Response</response>
        </dispatchOption>
    </dispatchOptions>
</dispatchConfig>
```

**Best Practices for Mock Services**

| Practice | Why |
|----------|-----|
| **Keep mocks simple** | Complex mocks are hard to maintain |
| **Document expected behavior** | Teams need to know mock capabilities |
| **Use realistic data** | Helps frontend development |
| **Simulate error conditions** | Test error handling paths |
| **Version your mocks** | Match API versions |
| **Start/stop in setup/teardown** | Clean test execution |
| **Use scripts sparingly** | They complicate debugging |

**Key Insight:** Mock services transform SoapUI from a testing tool into a development accelerator. By simulating APIs before they're built, teams can work in parallel, test edge cases safely, and verify contracts early. This is especially powerful in microservices architectures where dependencies abound.

content.title: Performance Testing Your APIs
content.explanation:
SoapUI includes built-in load testing capabilities that allow you to reuse your functional tests for performance testing. This ensures your APIs not only work correctly but also perform under load.

**Load Testing Concepts**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    LOAD TESTING FUNDAMENTALS                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                   │
│  ⏱️ Threads: Virtual users simulating real users                  │
│  📈 Ramp-Up: Gradually increasing load                           │
│  🔄 Loops: How many times each user executes                     │
│  ⏲️ Duration: How long the test runs                              │
│  📊 TPS: Transactions Per Second (throughput)                     │
│  ⚡ Response Time: How fast the API responds                       │
│  ❌ Error Rate: Percentage of failed requests                      │
│                                                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Creating a Load Test**

```
1. Right-click TestCase → New LoadTest
2. Name: "UserAPI Load Test"
3. Configure load strategy and limits
```

**Load Test Configuration**

```xml
<loadTest name="UserAPI Load Test" type="Simple">
    <!-- Thread Configuration -->
    <threadCount>10</threadCount>
    <startDelay>0</startDelay>
    <rampUp>30</rampUp> <!-- seconds to reach full load -->
    <testLimit>60</testLimit> <!-- test duration seconds -->
    
    <!-- Strategy -->
    <strategy>THREAD</strategy>
    
    <!-- Assertions -->
    <assertion type="Step">
        <configuration>
            <maxErrors>0</maxErrors>
            <maxErrorsPerStep>0</maxErrorsPerStep>
        </configuration>
    </assertion>
    
    <assertion type="TPS">
        <configuration>
            <minTps>5</minTps>
            <maxTps>100</maxTps>
        </configuration>
    </assertion>
    
    <assertion type="ResponseTime">
        <configuration>
            <maxResponseTime>500</maxResponseTime>
        </configuration>
    </assertion>
</loadTest>
```

**Load Strategies**

| Strategy | Description | Use Case |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| **Simple** | Fixed threads, configurable ramp-up | General load testing |
| **Variance** | Varies threads between min/max | Simulate fluctuating load |
| **Burst** | Periodic spikes in load | Event-driven systems |
| **Grid** | Distributed load testing | Large-scale tests |

**Variance Strategy Configuration**

```xml
<loadTest name="Variance Test" type="Variance">
    <threadCount>20</threadCount>
    <variance>10</variance> <!-- Vary ±10 threads -->
    <interval>5000</interval> <!-- Change every 5 seconds -->
    <testLimit>300</testLimit>
</loadTest>
```

**Burst Strategy Configuration**

```xml
<loadTest name="Burst Test" type="Burst">
    <threadCount>50</threadCount>
    <burstThreads>200</burstThreads> <!-- Spike to 200 -->
    <burstDuration>10</burstDuration> <!-- For 10 seconds -->
    <burstInterval>60</burstInterval> <!-- Every minute -->
    <testLimit>600</testLimit>
</loadTest>
```

**Load Test Assertions**

```xml
<!-- TPS Assertion (Transactions Per Second) -->
<assertion type="TPS">
    <configuration>
        <minTps>10</minTps>
        <maxTps>0</maxTps> <!-- 0 means no max -->
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Response Time Assertion -->
<assertion type="ResponseTime">
    <configuration>
        <maxResponseTime>500</maxResponseTime>
        <maxResponseTimePercent>95</maxResponseTimePercent>
    </configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- Step Assertion (errors) -->
<assertion type="Step">
    <configuration>
        <maxErrors>0</maxErrors>
        <maxErrorsPerStep>0</maxErrorsPerStep>
    </configuration>
</assertion>
```

**Running Load Tests**

```
# From UI
Open LoadTest → Click ▶️ (green play button)

# From command line
```bash
loadtestrunner.sh -s "UserAPITestSuite" \
                  -c "UserCRUD" \
                  -l "UserAPI Load Test" \
                  -r reports/ \
                  UserAPI-soapui-project.xml
```

**Load Test Statistics**

SoapUI provides real-time statistics during load tests:

| Statistic | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **TPS** | Transactions per second |
| **Avg Response Time** | Average response time |
| **Min/Max Response** | Fastest/slowest requests |
| **Error Count** | Number of failed requests |
| **Running Threads** | Current active threads |
| **Total Count** | Total requests executed |
| **Bytes In/Out** | Network throughput |
| **Percentiles** | 90th, 95th, 99th percentiles |

**Monitoring Load Tests**

```xml
<loadTest name="Monitored Test">
    <!-- Graph Statistics Configuration -->
    <graphStatistics>
        <statistic>TPS</statistic>
        <statistic>Average Response Time</statistic>
        <statistic>Error Count</statistic>
    </graphStatistics>
    
    <!-- History Points (how many data points to keep) -->
    <historyPoints>100</historyPoints>
</loadTest>
```

**Load Test Reports**

After execution, SoapUI generates comprehensive reports:

```
reports/
├── LoadTest-UserAPI-Load-Test-1.html  # HTML report
├── LoadTest-UserAPI-Load-Test-1.xml   # Raw data
└── LoadTest-UserAPI-Load-Test-1.png   # Statistics graph
```

**Load Test Scripting**

```groovy
// Groovy script in load test
import com.eviware.soapui.support.types.StringToObjectMap

// Access load test context
def loadTest = context.loadTest

// Get current statistics
def tps = loadTest.getStatistics().getTPS()
def avgResponse = loadTest.getStatistics().getAverageTime()
log.info "Current TPS: ${tps}, Avg Response: ${avgResponse}ms"

// Conditional stop if performance degrades
if (avgResponse > 1000) {
    log.warn "Response time too high, stopping test"
    loadTest.cancel()
}
```

**Distributed Load Testing**

For larger loads, SoapUI supports distributed testing:

```xml
<loadTest name="Distributed Test" type="Grid">
    <gridAgents>
        <agent host="loadagent1.company.com" port="8081"/>
        <agent host="loadagent2.company.com" port="8081"/>
    </gridAgents>
    <threadsPerAgent>50</threadsPerAgent>
    <testLimit>600</testLimit>
</loadTest>
```

**Load Test Best Practices**

| Practice | Why |
|----------|-----|
| **Start with small loads** | Validate before scaling |
| **Use realistic ramp-up** | Simulate real user arrival |
| **Monitor client resources** | Ensure load generator isn't bottleneck |
| **Set meaningful assertions** | Fail fast if performance degrades |
| **Run in dedicated environment** | Avoid interference |
| **Save raw data** | For later analysis |
| **Compare baselines** | Track performance trends |

**Load Test Interpretation**

```
Sample Results:
================
Total Threads: 50
Duration: 5 minutes
Total Requests: 15,234

TPS: 50.78 (target: 50)
Avg Response: 245ms (target: <300ms)
95th Percentile: 412ms (target: <500ms)
Error Rate: 0.2% (target: <1%)

Interpretation:
✅ Throughput meets target
✅ Average response time good
✅ 95th percentile acceptable
✅ Error rate within limits
```

**Key Insight:** Load testing in SoapUI leverages your existing functional tests, ensuring consistency between functional and performance testing. The built-in strategies and real-time monitoring make it easy to identify performance bottlenecks before they reach production.

content.title: Taking SoapUI to the Enterprise Level
content.explanation:
ReadyAPI is SmartBear's commercial API testing platform that builds on SoapUI's open-source foundation, adding powerful features for enterprise testing needs.

**ReadyAPI Components**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      READYAPI PLATFORM                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                   │
│  🚀 ReadyAPI (Core):                                            │
│  ├── SoapUI Pro (Enhanced functional testing)                   │
│  ├── Test Creation Wizard                                       │
│  ├── Data-Driven Testing                                        │
│  └── CI/CD Integration                                           │
│                                                                   │
│  ⚡ LoadUI Pro:                                                  │
│  ├── Advanced load testing                                      │
│  ├── Real-time analytics                                        │
│  ├── Cloud-based load generation                                │
│  └── Infrastructure monitoring                                  │
│                                                                   │
│  🛡️ ServiceV Pro:                                                │
│  ├── Service virtualization                                     │
│  ├── API simulation                                             │
│  └── Environment management                                     │
│                                                                   │
│  🔒 ReadyAPI Security Testing:                                   │
│  ├── Vulnerability scanning                                     │
│  ├── OWASP Top 10 checks                                        │
│  └── Security compliance                                        │
│                                                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Key ReadyAPI Features**

**1. Test Creation Wizard**

```
# Generate tests from API definitions
1. File → New Project → Import API
2. Select OpenAPI/Swagger, WSDL, or GraphQL
3. ReadyAPI automatically:
   - Creates functional test cases
   - Adds assertions for status codes
   - Validates response schemas
   - Sets up data-driven templates
```

**2. Data-Driven Testing Enhancements**

```xml
<!-- Data Source configuration in ReadyAPI -->
<dataSource name="ExcelDataSource">
    <configuration>
        <driver>Excel</driver>
        <file>C:/testdata/users.xlsx</file>
        <workbook>TestData.xlsx</workbook>
        <worksheet>Users</worksheet>
        <startRow>2</startRow>
        <endRow>0</endRow> <!-- 0 means all rows -->
        <columns>
            <column>name</column>
            <column>email</column>
            <column>role</column>
        </columns>
    </configuration>
    
    <!-- Data Source Loop automatically handles iteration -->
    <dataSourceLoop>
        <dataSource>ExcelDataSource</dataSource>
    </dataSourceLoop>
</dataSource>
```

**3. Test Recipes (Reusable Components)**

```xml
<!-- Save as recipe for reuse across projects -->
<testRecipe name="Authentication Flow">
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Login">
        <config>
            <endpoint>${#Project#authUrl}</endpoint>
            <resource>/login</resource>
            <method>POST</method>
            <request>
            {
                "username": "${#Recipe#username}",
                "password": "${#Recipe#password}"
            }
            </request>
        </config>
    </testStep>
    
    <testStep type="groovy" name="ExtractToken">
        <script>
            // Extract token and store as property
            def response = context.expand('${Login#Response}')
            def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
            testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue("authToken", json.token)
        </script>
    </testStep>
</testRecipe>
```

**4. CI/CD Integration**

```yaml
# Jenkins pipeline example
pipeline {
    agent any
    stages {
        stage('API Tests') {
            steps {
                script {
                    // Run ReadyAPI tests
                    bat """
                        "C:\\Program Files\\SmartBear\\ReadyAPI-3.49.0\\bin\\testrunner.bat" ^
                        -f reports ^
                        -R JUnit-Style-Html-Report ^
                        -e QA ^
                        -u admin ^
                        -p password123 ^
                        MyAPI-readyapi-project.xml
                    """
                }
            }
            post {
                always {
                    junit 'reports/*.xml'
                    publishHTML([reportDir: 'reports', 
                                reportFiles: '*-Report.html'])
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**5. Dashboard and Analytics**

ReadyAPI provides a web-based dashboard for:

- Test execution history
- Performance trends
- Team collaboration
- Test result analytics
- API coverage reports

**6. Security Testing Module**

```xml
<securityTest name="API Security Scan">
    <!-- Scan types -->
    <scan type="SQL Injection">
        <configuration>
            <payloads>
                <payload>' OR '1'='1</payload>
                <payload>; DROP TABLE users</payload>
            </payloads>
        </configuration>
    </scan>
    
    <scan type="XSS Injection">
        <configuration>
            <payloads>
                <payload><![CDATA[<script>alert(1)</script>]]></payload>
            </payloads>
        </configuration>
    </scan>
    
    <scan type="Malformed XML">
        <configuration>
            <payloads>
                <payload><![CDATA[<user><id>1</id><name>]]></payload>
            </payloads>
        </configuration>
    </scan>
    
    <scan type="Fuzzing">
        <configuration>
            <strategy>Garbage</strategy>
            <iterations>1000</iterations>
        </configuration>
    </scan>
</securityTest>
```

**7. LoadUI Pro Enhancements**

```xml
<loadTest name="Advanced Load Test">
    <!-- Cloud-based load generation -->
    <cloudAgents>
        <agent provider="aws" region="us-east-1" count="5"/>
        <agent provider="azure" region="westus" count="3"/>
    </cloudAgents>
    
    <!-- Real-time infrastructure monitoring -->
    <monitoring>
        <target type="server" host="api.example.com">
            <metric>CPU</metric>
            <metric>Memory</metric>
            <metric>Network</metric>
        </target>
    </monitoring>
    
    <!-- Advanced assertions -->
    <assertion type="Apdex">
        <configuration>
            <target>0.9</target>
            <tolerating>500</tolerating>
            <frustrating>2000</frustrating>
        </configuration>
    </assertion>
</loadTest>
```

**8. ServiceV Pro (Virtualization)**

```xml
<virtualService name="Payment API">
    <!-- Virtualize dependent services -->
    <virtualOperation method="POST" path="/process">
        <behavior>
            <!-- Rule-based responses -->
            <rule>
                <condition>${request.amount} > 1000</condition>
                <response>fraud-check.xml</response>
            </rule>
            <rule>
                <condition>${request.currency} == 'USD'</condition>
                <response>usd-success.xml</response>
            </rule>
            <default>success.xml</default>
        </behavior>
        
        <!-- Performance simulation -->
        <performance>
            <latency distribution="normal" mean="200" stddev="50"/>
            <throughput>100</throughput>
        </performance>
    </virtualOperation>
</virtualService>
```

**SoapUI vs ReadyAPI Comparison**

| Feature | SoapUI (Open Source) | ReadyAPI (Commercial) |
|---------|---------------------|----------------------|
| **Functional Testing** | ✅ Full | ✅ Enhanced |
| **Load Testing** | ✅ Basic | ✅ Advanced + Cloud |
| **Mock Services** | ✅ Basic | ✅ Advanced |
| **Security Testing** | ❌ | ✅ Full |
| **Data-Driven** | ✅ Manual | ✅ Wizard + Excel/DB |
| **CI/CD Integration** | ✅ Command line | ✅ Enhanced + Plugins |
| **Test Creation** | Manual | ✅ AI-assisted |
| **Reporting** | Basic | ✅ Advanced dashboards |
| **Support** | Community | ✅ Enterprise |

**When to Upgrade to ReadyAPI**

| Scenario | Why ReadyAPI |
|----------|--------------|
| **Security compliance required** | Built-in security scanning |
| **Large-scale load testing** | Cloud-based load generation |
| **Complex data scenarios** | Advanced data-driven features |
| **Enterprise support needed** | SLA-backed support |
| **CI/CD integration** | Native plugins for Jenkins, etc. |
| **Team collaboration** | Centralized dashboard |
| **Rapid test creation** | AI-assisted test generation |

**Key Insight:** ReadyAPI transforms SoapUI from a powerful tool into an enterprise platform. For teams scaling their API testing efforts, the commercial features—especially security testing, cloud-based load generation, and test data management—provide significant ROI. Start with open-source, upgrade when you hit its limits.

content.title: Writing Maintainable SoapUI Tests
content.explanation:
As your test suite grows, following best practices becomes essential for maintainability, reliability, and team collaboration.

**1. Use Properties for Configuration**

```xml
<!-- GOOD: Properties at project level -->
<properties>
    <property name="baseUrl" value="https://api.example.com/v1"/>
    <property name="timeout" value="30000"/>
    <property name="apiKey" value="${#Project#apiKey}"/>
</properties>

<!-- BAD: Hardcoded values everywhere -->
<endpoint>https://api.example.com/v1</endpoint>
<timeout>30000</timeout>
```

**2. Organize TestSuites by Functionality**

```
Project: ECommerceAPI
├── TestSuite: UserManagement
│   ├── TestCase: CreateUser
│   ├── TestCase: GetUser
│   └── TestCase: UpdateUser
├── TestSuite: ProductCatalog
│   ├── TestCase: SearchProducts
│   └── TestCase: GetProductDetails
└── TestSuite: OrderProcessing
    ├── TestCase: CreateOrder
    └── TestCase: CancelOrder
```

**3. Use Descriptive Naming**

```xml
<!-- GOOD -->
<testCase name="CreateUser_ValidData_Returns201">
<testCase name="CreateUser_MissingEmail_Returns400">
<testCase name="GetUser_InvalidID_Returns404">

<!-- BAD -->
<testCase name="Test1">
<testCase name="Test2">
<testCase name="Test3">
```

**4. Externalize Test Data**

```xml
<!-- GOOD: Data-driven with external file -->
<dataSource name="UserData">
    <configuration>
        <driver>Excel</driver>
        <file>${#Project#testDataDir}/users.xlsx</file>
    </configuration>
</dataSource>

<!-- BAD: Hardcoded in test case -->
<testStep name="CreateUser">
    <request>
    {
        "name": "John Doe",
        "email": "john@example.com"
    }
    </request>
</testStep>
```

**5. Reuse with Property Transfers**

```xml
<!-- GOOD: Extract and reuse -->
<testStep type="restrequest" name="CreateUser"/>
<testStep type="propertyTransfer" name="TransferUserID">
    <transfers>
        <transfer>
            <sourceStep>CreateUser</sourceStep>
            <sourcePath>$.id</sourcePath>
            <targetType>TestSuite</targetType>
            <targetName>userId</targetName>
        </transfer>
    </transfers>
</testStep>
<testStep type="restrequest" name="GetUser">
    <resource>/users/${#TestSuite#userId}</resource>
</testStep>
```

**6. Create Reusable Test Fragments**

```xml
<!-- Create reusable authentication test case -->
<testCase name="GetAuthToken" isDisabled="true">
    <testStep type="restrequest" name="Login">
        <request>
        {
            "username": "${#TestCase#username}",
            "password": "${#TestCase#password}"
        }
        </request>
    </testStep>
    <testStep type="groovy" name="ExtractToken">
        <script>
            def response = context.expand('${Login#Response}')
            def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
            testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue("authToken", json.token)
        </script>
    </testStep>
</testCase>

<!-- Use it in other tests -->
<testStep type="runTestCase" name="GetAuth">
    <targetTestCase>GetAuthToken</targetTestCase>
    <properties>
        <property name="username" value="admin"/>
        <property name="password" value="admin123"/>
    </properties>
</testStep>
```

**7. Use Assertions Wisely**

```xml
<!-- GOOD: Validate what matters -->
<assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes">
    <configuration><codes>200</codes></configuration>
</assertion>
<assertion type="JSONPath Existence">
    <configuration><path>$.id</path></configuration>
</assertion>
<assertion type="Response SLA">
    <configuration><sla>500</sla></configuration>
</assertion>

<!-- BAD: Over-asserting brittle data -->
<assertion type="Contains">
    <configuration><token>{"id":12345,"name":"John"}</token></configuration>
</assertion>
```

**8. Version Control Your Projects**

```
# Store in Git
UserAPI-soapui-project.xml

# Don't commit
*.backup
*.log
reports/
```

**9. Use Environment-Specific Configurations**

```xml
<!-- Global properties -->
<properties>
    <property name="dev.url" value="https://dev-api.example.com"/>
    <property name="qa.url" value="https://qa-api.example.com"/>
    <property name="prod.url" value="https://api.example.com"/>
    <property name="env" value="${#System#test.env}"/>
    <property name="baseUrl" value="${#Project#${#Project#env}.url}"/>
</properties>
```

**10. Implement Test Data Cleanup**

```xml
<testCase name="CleanupTestData">
    <!-- Always run even if tests fail -->
    <setupScript>
        // Mark this as cleanup case
    </setupScript>
    
    <testStep type="jdbc" name="DeleteTestUsers">
        <config>
            <query>
                DELETE FROM users 
                WHERE email LIKE 'test-%'
            </query>
        </config>
    </testStep>
</testCase>
```

**Common Pitfalls to Avoid**

| Pitfall | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| **Hardcoded endpoints** | Use project properties |
| **No cleanup after tests** | Implement teardown scripts |
| **Overly complex scripts** | Break into smaller steps |
| **Ignoring response times** | Add SLA assertions |
| **Not parameterizing test data** | Use DataSource |
| **Running all tests sequentially** | Use parallel execution |
| **No error handling** | Add conditional logic |

**SoapUI Performance Optimization**

```bash
# Increase memory in soapui.vmoptions
-Xms1024m
-Xmx2048m
-XX:MaxPermSize=512m

# Disable unused features
# File → Preferences → Disable animations
# Disable automatic validation
```

**Team Collaboration Tips**

1. **Share property files** - Keep `.properties` files in version control
2. **Document test cases** - Use description fields
3. **Standardize naming** - Create team naming conventions
4. **Peer review** - Review test cases before merging
5. **CI integration** - Run tests automatically on commits

**Key Insight:** SoapUI best practices are about making your tests **maintainable, reliable, and reusable**. The initial investment in structure pays dividends as your test suite grows from dozens to hundreds of test cases.

content.title: SoapUI Mastery Checklist
content.explanation:
A comprehensive checklist to guide your journey from SoapUI beginner to expert.

**Beginner Level (Week 1-2)**

```
□ Installed SoapUI and created first project
□ Imported WSDL/Swagger to generate requests
□ Created basic TestSuite with one TestCase
□ Added HTTP Status Code assertions
□ Ran a single request and viewed response
□ Used project properties for base URL
□ Created SOAP and REST requests
□ Added basic Contains assertions
□ Generated and viewed test reports
□ Ran tests from command line
```

**Intermediate Level (Week 3-4)**

```
□ Created multi-step test cases with property transfers
□ Used DataSource for Excel/CSV data-driven testing
□ Implemented Groovy scripts for custom logic
□ Added JSONPath and XPath assertions
□ Created Mock Services for dependent APIs
□ Used JDBC requests for database verification
□ Implemented conditional logic with Goto
□ Organized tests with meaningful naming
□ Used environment-specific properties
□ Created reusable test fragments
```

**Advanced Level (Week 5-8)**

```
□ Built comprehensive load tests with strategies
□ Implemented security scans for vulnerabilities
□ Created complex mock services with scripting
□ Used DataSink to export test results
□ Implemented CI/CD integration (Jenkins/GitHub)
□ Created custom assertions with Groovy
□ Used RunTestCase for test reuse
□ Implemented test data cleanup strategies
□ Mastered XPath and JSONPath for complex validation
□ Built parameterized test suites
```

**Expert Level (Months 2-3+)**

```
□ Designed enterprise test framework with ReadyAPI
□ Implemented distributed load testing
□ Created virtual services with ServiceV
□ Built custom SoapUI plugins/extensions
□ Integrated with APM and monitoring tools
